newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end Tokyo slightly firmer in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end Tokyo slightly firmer in thin trade.

text.p: Key March 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures closed slightly firmer in thin trade on Tuesday as demand for cash bonds overwhelmed large-lot selling in futures detected since Monday.
"Some people have been selling futures in large lots since yesterday. But despite that, the market"s downside was firmly protected," said a dealer with a city bank"s securities unit.
Steady buying was seen in cash JGBs including those with remaining maturities of seven years, traders said.
The March contract ended up 0.03 at 126.09 in small turnover of 38,377 contracts.
The key contract moved within a narrow range of between 125.95 and 126.18.

Another supportive factor was a retreat in the Tokyo stock market, traders said. The Nikkei 225 average ended its five-day rally on Tuesday when it closed 279.90 points or 1.49 percent down at the day"s low of 18,470.75.
"JGBs were bought because the stock market retreated. But the 0.23 yen range for the key March contract means that the market lacked energy to move," said a trust bank dealer.
Some traders said a flight to quality by some market participants continued to provide a support for JGBs.
Just before noon, Moody's Investors Service said it had placed placed Nippon Credit Bank Ltd"s Baa3 senior debt rating, including its debentures, under review for possible downgrade.
The rating agency also said it would review its senior debt ratings for the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB) and the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) for possible downgrade.

The announcement triggered dealers" selling in debentures issued by the banks, resulting in a rise of the yields by about three basis points, traders said. But NCB debentures remained mostly untraded due to a lack of interest, they said.
IBJ's January 1.6 percent five-year debenture was traded at a yield of 1.66 percent after Moody"s announcement, up from 1.63 percent on Tuesday morning, traders said.
A senior dealer at a securities house said selling in the afternoon was from dealers because it takes time before investors decide whether to change their investment stance.
"Dealers sold debentures to lighten their positions on their anticipation that they may have to buy these debentures from investors after tomorrow," he said.
Moody"s said while risks to NCB depositors in the medium term remained low, debenture holders faced "greater risks".

The MOF has said bank debentures issued by NCB and the other two long-term credit banks are not covered by Japan"s deposit insurance law. The chairman of the Federation of Bankers Associations of Japan said he agreed with MOF"s view.
Continuted buying in JGBs kept the yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB from rising above 2.4 percent. The yield was down 0.005 at 2.395 percent at 0717 GMT.

Yen bond trading was little affected by increasing concerns over the health of China"s paramount leader Deng Xiaoping as the foreign exchange market failed to react drastically, dealers said.-- Risa Maeda Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
